clue.text: Warm and sheltered place in carriage, on paper

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the Sun is a British daily newspaper
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone finds a cosy spot to sit, either in a carriage or somewhere described in print.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny spot shielded from wind is the classic garden or patio hideaway for basking.

clue.text: Reflecting about Democrat's disorderly party

indicators.note: the reflecting word goes about, round, the Democrat letter

parts.note: a shiny surface reflects light
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A politician thinks back on a Democratic party that got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflecting' suggests thinking back; here it means gleaming.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy brawl or rowdy celebration, an informal word for a commotion.

clue.text: Things getting bad with drug in club

indicators.note: the letters go bad, decaying into a new order

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Matters deteriorate at a nightclub where drugs are around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting bad' rearranges THINGS into NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub or venue for evening entertainment is called this.

clue.text: Disparage summary

definitions.meaning: a quick outline of the main points

explanation.surface: Belittle a brief account of events.
explanation.definitionFit: As a two-word verb it means criticise; as a noun it is a brief recap of points.

clue.text: Representation of art or play

indicators.note: a representation re-presents its subject, so the letters of the words are presented in a new order

explanation.surface: Something that depicts a painting or a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representation of' rearranges ART OR PLAY, and the whole clue describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Depicting something in painting, acting or writing is giving a depiction of it.

clue.text: Ancestor of today's queen, for example? Well, kind of

definitions.text: Ancestor of today's queen, for example?
definitions.meaning: a queen is a female cat, and the domestic cat descends from a wild feline species
an oil well sunk speculatively in unproven ground carries this name

explanation.surface: A question about the royal family tree, then a shrug of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' pretends to be royalty; in cat breeding a queen is an unneutered female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the untamed feline forebear of house pets and a speculative exploratory oil drilling.

clue.text: Power of Duke considerably reduced

definitions.meaning: British slang for force or effort, as in 'give it some'
the Duke of Wellington gave his name to the rubber boot, and this is that name much shortened

explanation.surface: A nobleman's influence has been cut back sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellington boot is named after the Duke of Wellington; its British pet name is the shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for vigour or oomph, and also the clipped informal name of the waterproof Wellington boot.

clue.text: Plant shot up, with so-called writer's support

indicators.note: in a down clue the writer's name sits below as support for the shot word

parts.note: a lob is a shot hit high into the air
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb, so the writer was so called

explanation.surface: A plant has shot upwards, propped up by a stake from someone who claims to be an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called' points to a pen name: Elia, under which Charles Lamb wrote his essays.
explanation.definitionFit: A low bedding flower, often blue, grown in borders and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Animal one spotted under cover

indicators.note: in a down clue the numeral goes below the cover word

parts.note: a coat is a covering layer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An animal is glimpsed hiding beneath a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-snouted raccoon relative of Central and South America.

clue.text: Get legal promotion of a sort, following particular approaches

indicators.note: the sort word comes after the approaches word

parts.note: takes are individual views or approaches, as in 'my take on it'
ilk means sort or kind, as in 'of that ilk'

explanation.surface: A lawyer gets a promotion of sorts after taking particular approaches to cases.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a barrister made King's or Queen's Counsel wears a silk gown, hence the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a barrister's appointment as senior counsel, entitled to wear a silk gown.

clue.text: Favoured strategist?. Not particularly

parts.note: to be in with someone, or in fashion, is to be favoured
a general is the military officer who plans strategy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a commander is popular, and gets a noncommittal reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means broadly or as a rule, the opposite of speaking of specifics.

clue.text: Bishop —- something needed for chess player

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for a bishop
a lack is a want, something one needs and has not got

explanation.surface: A bishop is named as one thing a chess game requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' looks part of the chess picture, but it only supplies its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the two sides are named by colour, and the player with the dark pieces takes that colour's name.

clue.text: What goes with gin and tonic, primarily, in party — same again

indicators.note: the drinks letters are placed inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
gin and it is a cocktail, 'it' being Italian vermouth

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word tonic is wanted

explanation.surface: At a party someone orders another gin and tonic, the same as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin and it' is a once-popular British drink of gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used to say the same thing again, as when repeating an order or statement.

clue.text: Appropriate payments for Henry James and Edward Lear?

definitions.text: Appropriate payments for Henry James and Edward Lear?

parts.words: Appropriate payments for Henry James and Edward Lear?
parts.note: authors are paid a share of sales, and Henry, James and Edward are also names of English kings

explanation.surface: A question about how two famous writers were paid for their books.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as writers they earn a cut of book sales; read as kings Henry, James and Edward are crowned heads, so the word suits them twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments to authors per copy sold, and also collectively a set of royal persons.

clue.text: Badly run play — defend such a sensational work

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre critic says a production was poorly managed while defending it as lurid entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges RUN PLAY DEFEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap lurid Victorian serial thriller was sold for a coin of small value, hence the name.

clue.text: In a hurry to come down, getting old candle

parts.note: rush means hurry
to light, or alight, is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: Someone hurries downstairs with an antique candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap historical candle made by dipping the pith of a rush plant in tallow.

clue.text: Grasping plump kind of pigeon

parts.note: fat means plump
a homing pigeon finds its way back to its loft

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a well-fed bird of the variety that flies home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasping' suggests greedy or clutching; here it means understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out the meaning of something, getting to the bottom of it, is understanding it.

clue.text: Western Europeans or one from North moving South

indicators.note: the South letter is shifted from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a Siberian comes from the far north of Asia

explanation.surface: Europeans in the west, or perhaps a northerner relocating to warmer parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' takes the S from the front of SIBERIAN and puts it at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, at Europe's western edge.

clue.text: Source of infinite fuel for place needing it eternally

definitions.meaning: a mine shaft with no floor would yield coal without end, and the phrase also describes a person with an endless appetite
hell, the abyss whose fires must burn for ever

explanation.surface: A riddle about a limitless fuel supply and a place that will always want it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is used of hell in the Bible and, informally, of someone who eats and eats without filling up.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss with no floor serves both as an endless store and as the fiery underworld of scripture.

clue.text: Serving monarch, like any worker, initially, in current rule

parts.note: OHMS stands for On His (or Her) Majesty's Service

indicators.note: the first letters of like, any and worker are taken

explanation.surface: A royal servant, like any employee, is bound by the current regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present'; here it means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics law relating voltage, electric current and resistance in a conductor.

clue.text: Constable eclipses one as extremely famous artist

indicators.note: to eclipse is to obscure by covering, so the constable letters surround the numeral

parts.note: PC is police constable
I is the Roman numeral one
so means very, extremely

explanation.surface: One famous painter, Constable, is outshone by another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' pretends to be the English painter John Constable; it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish cubist painter is among the best-known artists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Pale attempt to extend strike

definitions.meaning: a pointed wooden stake in a fence
a group stationed outside a workplace to dissuade others from working during industrial action

explanation.surface: A wan-looking effort to prolong a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence stake, and also strikers posted at a workplace gate to stop others going in.

clue.text: For example, a good person

parts.note: someone held up as an example for others to copy is a worthy person to imitate

explanation.surface: Someone illustrates a point by citing a virtuous individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like a throat-clearing phrase, but it is the clue: a person who serves as an example to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A person admired and imitated by others for their good conduct is described by this phrase.

clue.text: One of a couple left remaining

parts.note: over means left over, remaining

explanation.surface: One partner is the one left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Each partner in a romantic pair is the other's sweetheart.

clue.text: Intensity in part of France when it gets hot

parts.note: France is divided into administrative departments, abbreviated dept
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A region of France grows intense when the heat rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of colour or feeling means its richness or intensity.

clue.text: Bloomers made by one following dangerous reptile

indicators.note: the numeral letter comes after the reptile word

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone describes the blunders committed by a person trailing a crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests underwear or mistakes; here it means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a spring-flowering bulb, plants that bloom, so they are bloomers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Forging equipment found in Roman villa

indicators.note: the answer's letters are found inside the words Roman villa

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig up a blacksmith's tools in an ancient Roman house.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith hammers hot metal into shape on this heavy iron block, the essential tool of a forge.

clue.text: Toy requiring energy after work's over, by gum!

indicators.note: the energy word comes after the turned work word
the work word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
go means energy or vigour
to gum is to stick, fix with glue

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about a toy that needs energy once the working day is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns OP into PO; 'by gum!' looks like an old exclamation but STICK is gum's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-loaded pole that a child stands on and bounces about with is a familiar plaything.

clue.text: Said to be amazed, scatter wildly to ends of the earth

parts.note: to strew is to scatter untidily

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the phrase the earth are taken

explanation.surface: Someone said to be astonished flings things wildly to the four corners of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of the earth' gives the outer letters of the two-word phrase, T and H.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian and British exclamation of astonishment, a contraction of 'God's truth'.

clue.text: Had idea, but limited time

parts.note: though can mean but, however

explanation.surface: Someone came up with a plan, but there was too little time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' is a link: the time is limited to its single-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of think, so one who conceived a notion had it in mind.
